archetype.name: Playoff Team (glass-and-defense)
archetype.definition: A team whose rebounding and top-10 defense keep it comfortably in the playoff picture while its offense, a strength in recent seasons, has not yet caught up to that track record.

report.headline: Champions reboot on the glass while waiting for the jumpers to fall
report.take:
These are the reigning champions: 53-29 and 16 Playoff Wins last season. Nine games into the defense of that title they sit 5-4, third in the Atlantic behind Philadelphia and Boston, and 10th on the site. The record looks ordinary. The underlying profile is better than ordinary and also unlike last year's team. The 2025-26 Knicks won with the league's third-best offense. This version wins on the boards and on defense, and the offense has slid to 15th.

The glass is the identity. They lead the league in DRB % (77) and REB % (54.3) and are second in ORB % (32.3), all well above league average. Karl-Anthony Towns drives a lot of it, with 122 rebounds and a 66.6 TS %, and is fourth on the center tab. That is why the frontcourt grades an A while the backcourt and wings sit at C+. The defense ranks 7th with a 108.6 DRtg and is 7th in Opp Rim FG %. It gives up 104.22 points a game, third-fewest, though the slow pace (96) flatters that raw number. Opposing power forwards and centers have been shut down: PFs score well under their own averages against New York, the best mark in the league on that measure.

The offense is what the 5.9 Net Rtg hides. eFG % (51.1) and TS % (55.1) both rank 26th, against a 59 TS % last season. They are making threes at a good rate (36 3P %, 11th), so the problem is inside the arc and at the line, where their FT Rate ranks 22nd. Jalen Brunson carries a 31.8 USG % at a modest 54.2 TS %. The wings have given almost nothing on offense: Mikal Bridges is at 41.1 TS % with a -3.9 BPM. A shooting slump for a team that was a top-five offense for three straight years is more likely noise than a new identity.

The direction is already turning. October went 2-4 with points scored and allowed nearly even. November is 3-0, including a 30-point win over Chicago and a road win at Cleveland. Over the last five games they are 4-1 and +11.2 a game. The 46-win pace reads low for a team with this defense and rebounding and this pedigree. If the offense climbs back toward its usual level, they are a contender again rather than a playoff team.

strengths.title: League's best rebounding team
strengths.body: They lead the league in DRB % and REB % and rank second in ORB %, a margin over the league of several points on each. Towns' 122 rebounds anchor it, and Drummond's 70 in limited minutes keep it going when Towns sits. Rebounding is among the steadiest team traits, and this group was already strong on the glass last year, so expect it to last.

strengths.title: Top-10 defense that walls off the paint
strengths.body: The 108.6 DRtg ranks 7th, and opponents shoot just 62.1% at the rim, 7th-best. Opposing power forwards score well below their usual output, the best such mark in the league, and centers manage the fewest points of any team's. Last season's defense was also 7th, so this is a carried-over strength. The weak spot is pressure: the defense forces few turnovers and depends on contesting shots and finishing possessions with the rebound.

strengths.title: Towns playing at an elite level
strengths.body: Towns is 4th on the center tab, with a 66.6 TS % on a 25.2 USG %, a 4.7 BPM and a team-best 1.3 Win Shares. He is the most efficient high-usage scorer on a roster that has struggled to score efficiently. Efficiency that high usually cools a little, but he is the reason the frontcourt grades an A.

concerns.title: Shooting efficiency has fallen off
concerns.body: TS % of 55.1 and eFG % of 51.1 both rank 26th, two points below league average, after last season's 59 TS % drove the 3rd-ranked offense. The ORtg has slipped to 114.5, 15th. The three-point shooting is fine, so the problem is two-point finishing and few trips to the line. With three straight seasons of top-seven offenses behind them, expect a rebound, but it has to show up.

concerns.title: Wings giving little offense
concerns.body: Bridges is at a 41.1 TS % and -3.9 BPM, and the wing group has produced only 129 points combined while grading C+. Bridges' -22.3 On-Off and Anunoby's -26.1 are alarming, though on-off over nine games is noisy and both log heavy minutes. Hart, the best-ranked wing, is day-to-day. Opposing small forwards also take a larger share of the points against New York than the league norm, so the wings are a soft spot on defense too.

concerns.title: Brunson's load at modest efficiency
concerns.body: Brunson uses 31.8% of possessions at a 54.2 TS %, which is solid but not the engine a 3rd-ranked offense needs. His +8.6 On-Off shows the team still depends on him. If his efficiency does not climb back, the offense will stay around the league middle.

trend.note: A 2-4 October with scoring and allowing roughly even gave way to a 3-0 November, and the last five games are 4-1 at +11.2 a game, with the scoring up most.

weekAhead.headline: Two soft matchups, a rematch, then a division test
weekAhead.body:
Four games: home against Milwaukee and Cleveland on a back-to-back, then road trips to Indiana and Toronto. Milwaukee (1-9, 28th) and Indiana (3-7, 23rd) are the kind of teams this roster should beat on the glass. Milwaukee's DRB % ranks 27th and its defense 29th. Indiana is last in ORB % and 28th in REB %, with an F frontcourt. Cleveland, beaten 109-97 in Cleveland on Nov. 7, arrives on the second night of the back-to-back with an A- frontcourt and a 5th-ranked Opp eFG %. That is the game most likely to expose the half-court offense.

The week ends in Toronto, tied with New York at 5-4 in the division. The Raptors lead the league in ORB % and Opp TOV %, so this is the one opponent that can match the Knicks on the glass and pressure their ball handling. A 3-1 week is the reasonable expectation. A sweep would make the October start look like an early stumble.

keyMatchups.title: Towns against Milwaukee's soft middle
keyMatchups.body: Milwaukee allows centers far above their usual production, the worst mark in the league for points, rebounds and PRA relative to opponents' averages. Its frontcourt grades F. Towns at a 66.6 TS % should have a big night, and the home opener of the week is the place to restart the offense.

keyMatchups.title: Toronto's pressure vs. Knicks ball security
keyMatchups.body: Toronto forces turnovers on 17.7% of plays, the league's best rate. The Knicks protect the ball well, with a TOV % that ranks 7th. Toronto has held point guards well below their usual scoring, a test for Brunson. It gives up the most points to shooting guards, which opens the door for Shamet and McBride.

keyMatchups.title: Cleveland on the back-to-back
keyMatchups.body: The Cavs are a .500 team with a top-10 offense and a 5th-ranked Opp eFG %, and they will have seen New York four days earlier. The second night of a back-to-back against a stingy shooting defense tests whether the November uptick in scoring is real.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the Knicks' shooting efficiency climbs against Milwaukee and Indiana. A 26th-ranked TS % against two bottom-10 defenses would be a real warning sign.

restOfSeason.body:
The defense and rebounding look durable. Both are carried by Towns and a frontcourt grading A, and last year's team ranked 7th on defense with nearly the same rebounding profile. The offense is the swing. A 15th-ranked ORtg with a 26th-ranked TS % is out of line with a core that posted top-seven offenses for three straight seasons, so expect it to climb toward 115-118 points per 100. The current 46-win pace should rise with it. The record is roughly one win behind the margin, which is minor.

Two things cap the ceiling. The defense forces few turnovers, and Bridges and the rest of the wing production have to recover. If both come back, this is a 50-plus-win team and a real threat to defend the title. If the wings stay this weak, it is a solid playoff team that wins with rebounding and defense but cannot score efficiently enough to beat the top contenders.

confidence.note: Only nine games, with noisy on-off figures, but a strong multi-season track record.
